issues.legal_issue: An appellate court reviewing an acquittal must give due weight to the trial court’s assessment and cannot reverse a plausible acquittal without a reasoned reappraisal of the evidence.
material_facts: The trial court acquitted the accused after considering the disputed possession of the land, inconsistencies in the prosecution evidence, the ballistic report, and the possibility that others had fired weapons.
The High Court reversed the acquittal and convicted one accused, but its treatment of important evidentiary findings, including the ballistic evidence, was cryptic.
The Supreme Court found that the trial court’s view was plausible and that the High Court had not adequately reassessed the evidence before substituting its conclusions.
issues.conclusion: The High Court’s conviction was set aside and the trial court’s acquittal was restored.
issues.legal_principle: Under the principles stated in Sheo Swarup v. King Emperor and followed in decisions including Balbir Singh v. State of Punjab, Khedu Mohton v. State of Bihar, State of Goa v. Sanjay Thakran, and Murugesan v. State, an appellate court has power to review the evidence in an acquittal appeal but must give proper weight to the trial judge’s credibility findings, the presumption of innocence, the accused’s benefit of doubt, and the trial judge’s opportunity to see the witnesses. An appeal by an accused under Section 379 CrPC after a High Court reverses an acquittal is considered on parameters distinct from an ordinary appeal, as discussed in State of Rajasthan v. Abdul Mannan.

predicates.review_of_conviction_reversing_acquittal: The proceeding is an appeal against a conviction entered after an appellate court reversed a trial court acquittal.
predicates.trial_view_plausible: The trial court reached a reasonable view of the evidence after considering the material circumstances and discrepancies.
predicates.appellate_reappraisal_inadequate: The appellate court displaced the acquittal without adequately and reasonedly reassessing significant evidence and findings.

issues.definition: When a conviction reversing an acquittal is appealed, a plausible trial view combined with an inadequate appellate reappraisal results in the conviction being set aside and the acquittal restored.

issues.legal_issue: A material conflict between eyewitness evidence and ballistic evidence, particularly when the fatal shots are not connected to the accused’s weapon, can undermine the prosecution case and support reasonable doubt.
material_facts: The ballistic report showed that the cartridge cases recovered from the scene had not been fired from the weapon seized from the accused.
The report did not establish that the recovered pellets or the fatal injuries were caused by the seized weapon.
The prosecution’s eyewitness account attributed the shooting to the accused, but the forensic evidence did not connect the fatal shots to his weapon.
The High Court dismissed this conflict cryptically, and other evidence raised doubts about the prosecution account.
issues.conclusion: The ballistic conflict materially undermined the prosecution version and, considered with the other evidence, supported restoration of the acquittal.
issues.legal_principle: In Brijpal Singh v. State of Madhya Pradesh, a serious contradiction between eyewitness testimony and a ballistic report was treated as supporting reasonable doubt, particularly in light of weaknesses in the witnesses’ evidence and the absence of independent witnesses. Here, the Court held that the unconnected pellets and cartridge cases created a material contradiction that the High Court had failed to address adequately.

predicates.appeal_from_conviction_after_acquittal: The proceeding challenges a conviction entered after a trial court had acquitted the accused.
predicates.eyewitness_account_conflicts_with_ballis: The eyewitness account of the shooting materially conflicts with the forensic evidence about the firearms or ammunition used.
predicates.fatal_shots_unlinked_to_accused_weapon: The forensic evidence does not connect the fatal shots or recovered projectiles to the accused’s weapon.
predicates.prosecution_evidence_has_other_material_: Other significant features of the prosecution evidence also weaken its account of the incident.

issues.definition: In an appeal from a conviction after acquittal, a material eyewitness-ballistic conflict, an unconnected fatal weapon, and other material weaknesses mean that the prosecution case does not exclude reasonable doubt.

issues.legal_issue: The unexplained withholding of available witnesses who are essential to the prosecution account may support an adverse inference when the evidence already presented is not unimpeachable.
material_facts: The prosecution did not examine the deceased’s husband, who had been present from the beginning and could have clarified how the incident began.
The prosecution also did not examine three other witnesses said to have been injured, although they were available, and no explanation was given for their absence.
A key witness was interested in the outcome, making the missing witnesses’ evidence significant to the assessment of the prosecution case.
issues.conclusion: The non-examination of these material witnesses was significant in the circumstances and further weakened the prosecution case.
issues.legal_principle: Under State of Himachal Pradesh v. Gian Chand and Takhaji Hiraji v. Thakore Kubersing Chamansing, non-examination of a witness is not automatically fatal. An adverse inference may arise where an available witness could have disclosed the genesis or an essential part of the case, could have filled a gap, and was withheld without adequate explanation; it may not arise where reliable and unimpeachable evidence already establishes the case. Manjit Singh v. State of Punjab likewise emphasizes the quality and trustworthiness of the evidence rather than the number of witnesses.

predicates.prosecution_case: The proceeding is a criminal prosecution in which the prosecution relies on evidence to establish the accused’s guilt.
predicates.available_essential_witnesses_withheld_w: The prosecution does not call available witnesses whose testimony could clarify the genesis or an essential part of its case, and gives no adequate reason for their absence.
predicates.existing_evidence_not_unimpeachable: The evidence already presented is not so reliable and convincing that the missing testimony would merely be repetitive.

issues.definition: When a prosecution withholds available essential witnesses without explanation and its existing evidence is not unimpeachable, an adverse inference against the prosecution is warranted.

issues.legal_issue: A trial court’s limited finding that the prosecution had not established a forcible entry onto disputed land may be plausible where possession was contested and the evidence did not show that possession had been delivered to the complainant side.
material_facts: Possession of the land was the subject of a dispute between the accused and a separate organization.
There was no evidence that possession had been delivered to the complainant or the complainant’s family under the relevant local resolution.
The combine harvester was already on the land before the day of the occurrence.
The trial court used these circumstances to reject the allegation that the accused had forcibly entered the land and installed the harvester.
issues.conclusion: The trial court’s finding on the absence of a forcible entry was plausible for that limited purpose and could not be faulted merely by treating motive as immaterial.
issues.legal_principle: The Court stated that proof of intention is unnecessary when there is direct evidence, but held that the trial court’s assessment of possession remained relevant to whether the accused had forcibly entered the land and to its evaluation of the prosecution account. An appellate court must assess that finding in the context of the evidence and the applicable principles governing review of acquittals.

predicates.review_of_acquittal: The court is reviewing a trial court’s decision to acquit the accused.
predicates.possession_contested: The parties’ competing claims to possession of the relevant land were disputed.
predicates.no_evidence_possession_delivered_to_comp: The evidence did not show that possession of the land had been delivered to the complainant side.
predicates.alleged_object_already_on_land_before_in: The object said to have been installed through forcible entry was already on the land before the incident.

issues.definition: In review of an acquittal, contested possession, no evidence of delivery to the complainant side, and the object’s prior presence on the land make the limited finding of no forcible entry plausible.
